chunks: And a group of scholars narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Aswad al-Qummi narrated to me that Abu Ja'far al-Amari (may his spirit be sanctified) dug a grave for himself and leveled it with a marble slab. I asked him about that, and he said: 'For the people, there are reasons.' And I asked him about that, and he said: 'I have been ordered to gather my affairs.' He died two months after that. May Allah be pleased with him and may He please him.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الْعَمَرِيُّ: Abu Ja'far al-Amari, a specific historical figure and emissary
key_terms.أَنْ أَجْمَعَ أَمْرِي: to gather my affairs (a phrase indicating preparation for death or finalizing one's state)
key_terms.السَّاجِ: a marble slab (used for leveling graves)

ai.seo_question: Why did Abu Ja'far al-Amari dig his own grave before his death?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the spiritual preparedness of Abu Ja'far al-Amari, one of the Four Special Emissaries, who prepped his grave with a marble slab to demonstrate readiness for death. His response, 'I have been ordered to gather my affairs,' reflects the Shia concept of *jam' al-amr* (consolidating one's spiritual state) before the final transition, underscoring the importance of mindful departure during the Minor Occultation. This act serves as a practical model for believers to maintain constant awareness of mortality and divine command.
